title: Section 22 of Oaxaca in Favor of Continuing CNTE Strike; National Leadership Defines Course of Walkout Today
author: Carolina Gómez and Jessica Xantomila
content:
_This article by Carolina Gómez and Jessica Xantomila originally appeared in
the[June 13, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/06/13/politica/seccion-22-de-
oaxaca-continuara-huelga-de-la-cnte-dirigencia-nacional-define-hoy-el-rumbo-
del-paro), Mexico's premier left-wing daily newspaper._

Amid the consultation that the National Coordinator of Education Workers
(CNTE) is carrying out with its base mobilized in the National Strike, Section
22 of Oaxaca, which is one of those with the largest contingents on strike,
came out in favor of continuing the movement, which includes an encampment in
Mexico City's Historic Center, as well as marches and blockades in the
country's capital and in other states.

In the early hours of this morning at the Permanent State Assembly of Section
XXII SNTE-CNTE, Yenny Aracely Pérez Martínez, general secretary of the
section, reported that Oaxaca declares itself in favor of continuing the
movement, which began this past June 1, in the context of the 2026 FIFA World
Cup.

The results of the consultation were 6,162 votes for a recess of the strike
and 6,337 to continue the actions.

Likewise, since yesterday afternoon, Filiberto Fraustro, general secretary of
the Zacatecas section, was anticipating that the majority of the Coordinator's
teaching base in that state was in a "predisposition to continue" with the
actions of the national strike, but warned that they still had to wait for
what teachers in the other states decided.

The launch of the consultation stems from the agreements of the session of the
National Representative Assembly (ANR), held in the early hours of Friday.

If the rank-and-file conclude the consultation this Saturday, the results
could be announced at the ANR that is expected to take place today at midday.

Originally, that assembly had been called for midnight, but it was moved to
today.
